Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)


Shared reconstruction procedure:
Produce a compact, complete first build immediately; do not spend a separate turn on planning.
In brief code comments record the dominant silhouettes, approximate normalized image bounds,
main perspective directions, occlusion order, and camera hypothesis. These are estimates,
not measured calibration. Put camera, major dimensions and placement parameters together.
First establish architecture, every prominent object, essential supports, large color regions,
and a plausible camera. Keep semantic objects as named Assets with all their constituent
parts inside them. Preserve separate meshes and editable material assignments.

Reliability requirements derived from the actual SceneAct implementation:
- include(name,node) REPLACES an existing child with that name. Use unique indexed names
  inside loops. Include the returned node if subsequently editing an attachment that was cloned.
- fillet_box requires 0 < radius <= min(size)/2, INCLUDING thickness. Choose a valid radius
  explicitly; do not alter the library. It emits up to 23 primitive meshes per call.
- sweep_tube with N points emits N spheres and N-1 cylinders. Use few control points;
  adjacent points must differ. Use rod for straight members. Avoid dense ornamental sweeps.
- All dimensions and coordinates must be finite; dimensions and radii must be positive.
- realize clears Blender, including its world. After realize, before accessing world nodes:
  sc = bpy.context.scene
  if sc.world is None:
      sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('Ambient')
  sc.world.use_nodes = True
  Then configure Background, camera and lighting. Do not retain pre-realize bpy references.
- All geometry must use SceneAct. bpy is for materials, lighting and camera customization;
  do not bypass the geometry interface with direct mesh or curve creation.

Count expanded primitives, not helper calls. Aim for roughly 200-350 meshes initially and
keep revisions below roughly 500 unless essential visible structure requires more. These are
planning targets, not reasons to omit major objects or supports. Avoid thousands of floor
boards, fabric stitches or repeated tiny marks; use restrained procedural materials for
surface patterns. Use a small reusable material palette. Prefer simple assemblies over
Boolean operations. Before realize, print the actual primitive count using
sum(n.solid is not None for n in scene.traverse()). Never render additional views, save files,
or change the fixed runner's resolution, engine, sampling or other resource settings.

After a successful rendering, compare it with the original using 5-8 stable visible anchors:
major object extremes, wall/floor intersections and distinctive foreground/background points.
Distinguish global perspective/framing errors from local object size or placement errors.
Correct camera using scene-wide evidence; change individual objects only for local residuals.
Keep camera fixed when revising material/light appearance. Prefer one coherent correction
family per revision, preserving already matched anchors. Do not add fine detail while major
silhouettes, occlusion, framing or brightness remain wrong. Never infer improvement without
an actual render. A noisy render alone does not authorize changing fixed renderer settings.

On execution failure, there is no rendered view to compare. Repair the reported cause and
audit the other reliability requirements before returning a complete replacement. On timeout,
substantially simplify repeated surface detail and primitive expansion while retaining major
objects and semantic groups. With little time or the final execution, prioritize a valid,
compact scene over ornament. DONE is allowed only after a successful visible render.

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy, math

# Chaise bounds approximately (0.035,.24)-(.83,.93); tall back at upper left,
# rounded foot at lower right. Wall panels behind; cropped cane chair at lower left.
# Long rails recede toward image left. Camera looks downward from front/right.
scene = Scene('French chaise interior')
CAMERA = (3.0, -5.5, 3.7)
TARGET = (-.02, .12, .86)
cream = (.69,.66,.55)
linen = (.82,.77,.65)
wood = (.30,.36,.29)
gilt = (.59,.54,.39)
wall = (.72,.70,.63)

architecture = Asset('Paneled cream room')
architecture.include('floor', box((9,8,.12), center=(0,0,-.075), color=(.24,.125,.065)))
architecture.include('back_wall', box((8,.15,3.5), center=(0,1.14,1.7), color=wall))
architecture.include('right_return', box((.17,2.3,3.5), center=(2.27,2.2,1.7), color=(.77,.75,.68)))
for i,(z,h,d) in enumerate(((.08,.12,.07),(.20,.035,.042),(.37,.045,.035),(1.54,.055,.048),(1.65,.03,.035),(1.94,.07,.05),(2.12,.035,.04))):
    architecture.include('horizontal_molding_%d'%i, box((8,d,h),center=(0,1.035,z),color=(.80,.78,.70)))
# Large recessed rectangular panel outlines.
for j,(left,right) in enumerate(((-3.0,-1.45),(-1.40,1.82))):
    for k,delta in enumerate((0,.026)):
        yy=1.048-.012*k
        for n,z in enumerate((.43+delta,1.48-delta)):
            architecture.include('panel_%d_%d_h%d'%(j,k,n),box((right-left-2*delta,.025,.018),center=((left+right)/2,yy,z),color=(.79,.77,.69)))
        for n,x in enumerate((left+delta,right-delta)):
            architecture.include('panel_%d_%d_v%d'%(j,k,n),box((.018,.025,1.05-2*delta),center=(x,yy,.955),color=(.79,.77,.69)))
for i,x in enumerate((-1.55,.22,1.96)):
    architecture.include('wall_seam_%d'%i,box((.009,.007,3.0),center=(x,1.056,1.5),color=(.43,.42,.35)))
scene.include('architecture',architecture)

# Restrained parquet boards, with alternating grain directions.
floorboards=Asset('Parquet surface')
for i in range(10):
    for j in range(6):
        x=-3.6+i*.72
        y=-2.5+j*.60
        c=(.255+.012*((i+2*j)%4),.143+.009*((i+j)%3),.083)
        p=box((.70,.585,.012),center=(x,y,-.007),color=c)
        floorboards.include('board_%d_%d'%(i,j),p)
scene.include('parquet',floorboards)

chaise=Asset('Antique painted chaise longue')
# Upholstered seat with softly rounded end.
chaise.include('seat_cushion',fillet_box((2.28,.91,.27),radius=.132,center=(.03,0,.735),color=linen))
chaise.include('under_seat',fillet_box((2.22,.88,.12),radius=.055,center=(0,0,.575),color=wood))
# Upholstered tall curved headboard.
back=ball(1,center=(-1.04,.025,1.12),color=linen)
back.resize((.14,.49,.49))
back.turn('y',-13)
chaise.include('padded_back',back)
# Top bow and side posts around the back.
bow=[(-.98,-.46,.71),(-1.11,-.48,1.12),(-1.20,-.43,1.49),
     (-1.23,-.22,1.62),(-1.23,.10,1.64),(-1.18,.38,1.54),
     (-1.08,.46,1.27),(-.94,.46,.78)]
chaise.include('back_frame',sweep_tube(points=bow,radius=.032,color=wood))
chaise.include('back_gilded_edge',sweep_tube(points=[(x+.016,y-.014,z+.014) for x,y,z in bow],radius=.010,color=gilt))
# The near upholstered arm rises at the head, then sweeps into the seat.
arm=ball(1,center=(-.81,-.433,.965),color=linen)
arm.resize((.36,.063,.30))
arm.turn('y',-24)
chaise.include('near_side_upholstery',arm)
armline=[(-1.18,-.47,1.43),(-1.07,-.49,1.24),(-.91,-.49,1.12),
         (-.63,-.49,1.045),(-.50,-.49,.80),(-.44,-.49,.61)]
chaise.include('near_arm_wood',sweep_tube(points=armline,radius=.030,color=wood))
chaise.include('near_arm_trim',sweep_tube(points=[(x,y-.023,z+.012) for x,y,z in armline],radius=.009,color=gilt))
fararm=[(-1.17,.45,1.47),(-.98,.46,1.26),(-.70,.46,1.16),(-.61,.46,.87)]
chaise.include('far_arm',sweep_tube(points=fararm,radius=.026,color=wood))
# Carved apron follows the visible long edge.
for side in (-1,1):
    yy=side*.443
    pts=[(-1.02,yy,.60),(-.77,yy,.57),(-.36,yy,.565),(.12,yy,.535),(.58,yy,.54),(1.02,yy,.56),(1.13,yy,.49)]
    chaise.include('apron_%d'%side,sweep_tube(points=pts,radius=.043,color=wood))
    chaise.include('apron_edge_%d'%side,sweep_tube(points=[(x,y+side*.031,z+.025) for x,y,z in pts],radius=.009,color=gilt))
# Four cabriole legs, including splayed feet.
for i,x in enumerate((-.91,.98)):
    for j,y in enumerate((-.36,.36)):
        pts=[(x,y,.58),(x+.035,y,.43),(x-.035,y,.24),(x-.06,y-.025,.085),(x+.005,y-.035,.055)]
        chaise.include('leg_%d_%d'%(i,j),sweep_tube(points=pts,radius=.031,color=wood))
        chaise.include('leg_inlay_%d_%d'%(i,j),sweep_tube(points=[(a,b-.025,c) for a,b,c in pts[:-1]],radius=.008,color=gilt))
# Small carved floral medallions.
for i,x in enumerate((-.96,.12,1.04)):
    z=.55 if i!=1 else .515
    for k in range(5):
        a=k*math.tau/5
        node=ball(.025,center=(x+math.cos(a)*.038,-.487,z+math.sin(a)*.027),color=gilt)
        node.resize((1,.42,.8))
        chaise.include('carving_%d_%d'%(i,k),node)
# Pillow resting diagonally against the tall back.
pillow=fillet_box((.27,.64,.65),radius=.125,center=(-.87,-.015,1.18),color=(.86,.80,.67))
pillow.turn('y',-22)
pillow.turn('x',-9)
chaise.include('loose_cream_pillow',pillow)
# Green museum label on the seat.
label=box((.085,.15,.005),center=(.72,.10,.877),color=(.055,.22,.18))
label.turn('z',-7)
chaise.include('green_label',label)
for k in range(3):
    chaise.include('label_print_%d'%k,box((.037,.004,.002),center=(.72,.07+k*.019,.881),color=(.73,.75,.60)))
scene.include('chaise',chaise)

curtains=Asset('Window and ivory drapes')
curtains.include('window_glow',box((.035,1.4,3.3),center=(-1.66,.28,1.6),color=(.94,.94,.86)))
for i in range(8):
    x=-1.61+.027*math.sin(i*1.4)
    y=-.55+i*.092
    curtains.include('curtain_fold_%d'%i,rod(.052,start=(x,y,.07),end=(x-.07,y,2.8),color=(.80+.012*(i%3),.77+.013*(i%3),.67+.02*(i%3))))
scene.include('curtains',curtains)

foreground=Asset('Cropped cane chair')
# A partial secondary chair enters the lower left corner.
chairseat=fillet_box((.64,.63,.07),radius=.033,center=(-1.28,-1.32,.45),color=wood)
foreground.include('seat_frame',chairseat)
foreground.include('woven_seat',box((.54,.53,.022),center=(-1.28,-1.32,.494),color=(.47,.33,.20)))
for i in range(15):
    x=-1.53+i*.035
    foreground.include('cane_x_%d'%i,rod(.003,start=(x,-1.565,.510),end=(x,-1.075,.510),color=(.70,.57,.36)))
for i in range(14):
    y=-1.55+i*.035
    foreground.include('cane_y_%d'%i,rod(.003,start=(-1.535,y,.513),end=(-1.025,y,.513),color=(.68,.54,.34)))
for i,x in enumerate((-1.53,-1.03)):
    foreground.include('leg_%d'%i,rod(.028,start=(x,-1.50,.03),end=(x,-1.50,.46),color=wood))
scene.include('foreground_chair',foreground)

print('Primitive count:',sum(n.solid is not None for n in scene.traverse()))
realize(scene)

# Procedural woven fabric; small rose motifs on parallel upholstery stripes.
fabric=bpy.data.materials.new('Ivory woven striped floral upholstery')
fabric.diffuse_color=(*linen,1)
fabric.use_nodes=True
nodes=fabric.node_tree.nodes
links=fabric.node_tree.links
bs=nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=.86
tex=nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
sep=nodes.new('ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ')
links.new(tex.outputs['Generated'],sep.inputs[0])
wave=nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexWave')
wave.wave_type='BANDS'
wave.bands_direction='Y'
wave.inputs['Scale'].default_value=18
wave.inputs['Distortion'].default_value=.3
links.new(tex.outputs['Generated'],wave.inputs['Vector'])
ramp=nodes.new('ShaderNodeValToRGB')
ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=.68
ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=(.81,.76,.65,1)
ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position=.78
ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=(.59,.46,.40,1)
links.new(wave.outputs['Color'],ramp.inputs[0])
noise=nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
noise.inputs['Scale'].default_value=150
noise.inputs['Detail'].default_value=2
links.new(tex.outputs['Generated'],noise.inputs['Vector'])
bump=nodes.new('ShaderNodeBump')
bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.15
bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value=.008
links.new(noise.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height'])
links.new(bump.outputs['Normal'],bs.inputs['Normal'])
links.new(ramp.outputs['Color'],bs.inputs['Base Color'])
for obj in bpy.context.scene.objects:
    if obj.type=='MESH' and any(s in obj.name.lower() for s in ('seat_cushion','padded_back','near_side_upholstery')):
        obj.data.materials.clear()
        obj.data.materials.append(fabric)

sc=bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world=bpy.data.worlds.new('Ambient')
sc.world.use_nodes=True
sc.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[0].default_value=(.65,.68,.72,1)
sc.world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[1].default_value=.45
set_view(CAMERA,TARGET,lens=48)
area_emitter((-3,-1,3.4),power=650,size=3.0,target=(0,0,.7),color=(1,.94,.82))
area_emitter((1,-3,3.6),power=130,size=3,target=(0,0,.8),color=(1,.95,.88))
sc.view_settings.view_transform='AgX'
```
